verses.1:
For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies.” A Maskil + 45:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142. of the sons of Korah. A love song.
 My heart is stirred by a noble theme
 as I recite my verses to the king; + 45:1 Or King ; here and throughout Psalm 45 
 my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer.
verses.3:
Strap your sword at your side, O mighty warrior;
 appear in your majesty and splendor.
verses.5:
Your arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s foes;
 the nations fall beneath your feet.
verses.6:
Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever,
 and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.
verses.7:
You have loved righteousness
 and hated wickedness;
 therefore God, your God, has anointed you
 above your companions with the oil of joy. + 45:7 Cited in Hebrews 1:8–9|HEB 1:8-9
verses.10:
Listen, O daughter! Consider and incline your ear:
 Forget your people and your father’s house,
verses.11:
and the king will desire your beauty;
 bow to him, for he is your lord.
verses.12:
The Daughter of Tyre will come with a gift;
 men of wealth will seek your favor.
verses.13:
All glorious is the princess in her chamber;
 her gown is embroidered with gold.
verses.14:
In colorful garments she is led to the king;
 her virgin companions are brought before you.
verses.15:
They are led in with joy and gladness;
 they enter the palace of the king.
verses.16:
Your sons will succeed your fathers;
 you will make them princes throughout the land.
verses.17:
I will commemorate your name through all generations;
 therefore the nations will praise you forever and ever.

metadata.source: Derived from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB). Missing verses restored from the Textus Receptus tradition for completeness.
